stories.primary_headline: One month of IIT Bombay student's death: No arrests yet; protest continues

primary_source.headline: One month of IIT Bombay student's death: No arrests yet; protest continues
primary_source.content: Mumbai: Exactly a month after Sahil Wakode, a student of Indian Institute of Technology-Bombay died by suicide, students and activists staged a protest outside the institute’s Powai campus on Sunday, however, police dispersed the mob and detained several of them.The parents of Sahil—Ravindra Wakode and Sonali Wakode—too were part of the protests.&nbsp;On 18 September, Sahil (20), a second-year student from Energy Science and Engineering Department, was caught allegedly using a mobile phone to access ChatGPT during a mid-semester examination. However, his body was later found in his hostel room.&nbsp;The case is being investigated by the&nbsp;Crime Branch-CID, which has taken over investigations from the Powai police station.&nbsp;Sahil Wakode death: Protesting IIT Bombay students claim detention, use of excessive force by policeThe parents are demanding action and arrest of&nbsp; Prof Shireesh Kedare, the Director of&nbsp; Indian Institute of Technology-Bombay and Prof Suryanarayana Doolla, a faculty member of the premier institute’s Energy Science and Engineering Department.Meanwhile, the Congress once again backed the parents and said that it will ensure that Sahil Wakode gets justice. Sahil Wakode, a backward-class student at the IIT Mumbai institution, did not commit suicide; it was "an institutional murder."“Even though a month has passed since this incident, no action has been taken against anyone yet. In the past 13 months, 4 students in this institution have died by suicide. After Sahil's death, students in the institution are protesting, and the police are committing atrocities against them, beating them. On whose orders are the police committing atrocities in the institution's premises? All these things must stop. An inquiry must be conducted quickly, and strict action must be taken against those responsible for Sahil's murder,” said Mumbai Congress president and MP Prof Varsha Gaikwad.&nbsp;“RSS ideology has infiltrated this prestigious IIT institution, and this is not good for the education sector. Keep educational institutions away from political ideologies,” she added.&nbsp;A delegation from the All India Independent Scheduled Castes Association arrived at the IIT Bombay gates around noon, seeking to pay respects to Sahil.&nbsp;

stories.primary_headline: Sahil Wakode death: Protesting IIT Bombay students claim detention, use of excessive force by police

primary_source.headline: Sahil Wakode death: Protesting IIT Bombay students claim detention, use of excessive force by police
primary_source.content: Mumbai: Twenty-two IIT Bombay students, including eight who were allegedly detained twice in a single day, were picked up by the police from inside the campus on Sunday amid their ongoing protest demanding justice for deceased Sahil Wakode, student bodies said.The protesters and student collectives alleged that police used extreme force during the crackdown, accusing the cops of tearing their clothes, kicking and choking them. All detained students were taken to the Powai police station, they said.Police and IIT B authorities are yet to issue a detailed official statement regarding the scale of the detentions and the allegations of excessive force.Students have been protesting near the campus gates in the Powai area for a month, including a 15-day hunger strike, raising allegations of caste discrimination and institutional apathy surrounding the death of 22-year-old Sahil Wakode.IIT Bombay suicide: Sahil Wakode apologised for cheating in exam, sought second chance, say policeThe second-year B.Tech student was found dead in his hostel room on September 18 after allegedly being caught cheating during a mid-semester exam. Sunday marked one month since his alleged suicide, prompting students to plan a memorial and a ‘mashal juloos’ (torchlight procession).Student representatives alleged that police barged into the campus in large numbers in the morning. After an initial detention and brief release, students gathered at the protest site, alongside Wakode’s grieving parents to pay tribute, they said.Protesters alleged that the campus security and police subsequently dismantled the protest site and forcibly removed the participants. They also claimed that female students faced inappropriate touching and physical assault. A total of 22 students were detained, they said.The demonstrators also targeted the IIT Bombay administration over the deployment of police inside the campus, asking who authorised it.Congress MP Varsha Gaikwad and representatives of several Ambedkarite organisations subsequently reached the spot and staged a demonstration demanding an immediate meeting with the Chairperson of the Board of Governors and the Director.While officials from the Powai police station were not immediately available for comment, the institute authorities were yet to share their response to the detentions and allegations of excessive force.Wakode’s parents have been continuing their hunger strike at Azan Maidan in south Mumbai, demanding action and accountability from the institute administration.They have accused Professor Suryanarayana Doolla of harassment and caste-based discrimination. Earlier this month, the police questioned Doolla for nearly 10 hours in connection with the alleged suicide.

stories.primary_headline: The problem with telling people the world is ending

primary_source.headline: The problem with telling people the world is ending
primary_source.content: In the face of terrible crises, it can feel right to shock people into action. But what if that has the opposite effect?These days, it’s easy to succumb to hopelessness. Whether you’re thinking about the climate crisis, the prospect of AI apocalypse, war or political turmoil, the list of challenges facing humanity can seem insurmountable.It certainly feels unprecedented, and much of it may be. The sense of impending doom, on the other hand, is nothing new. And what we have learned from the past is that doomerism can lead to paralysis. If everyone freezes, then nothing changes – but if we want to have a chance of mitigating some of the threats I’ve mentioned then action is what’s required. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: G7 to launch exercises to guard against AI cyber attacks

primary_source.headline: G7 to launch exercises to guard against AI cyber attacks

sources.headline: G7 to launch exercises to guard against AI cyber attacks

brief_bullets: The Group of Seven (G7) nations have announced a coordinated initiative to launch large-scale simulation exercises designed to bolster collective defenses against sophisticated cyberattacks powered by artificial intelligence. This strategic move, spearheaded by member nations, aims to address the escalating threat landscape where malicious actors increasingly leverage generative AI to automate phishing campaigns, develop polymorphic malware, and execute high-velocity data breaches. By conducting these rigorous stress tests, the G7 intends to harmonize incident response protocols, enhance cross-border information sharing, and identify critical vulnerabilities within shared digital infrastructure. This collaborative framework reflects a growing consensus among global leaders that traditional cybersecurity measures are insufficient against the speed and adaptability of AI-driven threats. Ultimately, the exercises serve as a proactive mechanism to ensure that democratic economies remain resilient against state-sponsored and criminal cyber operations that threaten global financial stability and national security. This initiative marks a pivotal shift toward proactive, multilateral cyber-defense, signaling that G7 nations are prioritizing the standardization of AI-security protocols to prevent systemic digital collapse. It establishes a new geopolitical benchmark for how advanced economies must integrate defensive AI capabilities to counter the asymmetric advantages currently enjoyed by sophisticated cyber adversaries.

brief_bullets: Microsoft has officially withdrawn as the anchor tenant for a massive AI datacentre project in Loughton, Essex, citing significant concerns regarding the reliability and availability of local power supplies. Developed by the British firm Nscale, the facility was previously championed by UK government ministers as the nation’s largest AI-focused infrastructure project, intended to bolster domestic technological capacity by 2026. This sudden departure represents a major setback for the development, which relied heavily on Microsoft’s commitment to justify its scale and operational viability. The decision highlights the growing friction between the UK’s ambitious AI industrial strategy and the practical limitations of its aging national energy grid. As demand for high-density computing power surges, this project’s instability underscores the critical infrastructure bottlenecks that threaten to impede the country's aspirations to become a global leader in artificial intelligence. The project's collapse exposes a critical vulnerability in the UK's digital infrastructure strategy, where energy grid capacity is failing to keep pace with the massive power requirements of modern AI datacentres. This failure risks deterring future foreign investment and stalling the government's broader economic goals for the technology sector.

This failure risks deterring future foreign investment and stalling the government's broader economic goals for the technology sector.
